$comment: Lane C's verified copy of contracts/harness-presets.json (tk session 0's skeleton, 27 Oct 2026), filled and checked on 27 Oct 2026 against each harness's own docs or source at the version named in `sources`, and where the CLI could be installed in the cloud, against what its own `mcp add` wrote into a scratch HOME (crates/tk-cli/src/connect/fixtures/recorded/). Marks inside strings: (V) read in a primary source or run; (I) inference; (NF) searched, not found. `tokens` in paths: ~ is the home folder; <project> the project root. Fields added to the skeleton: format, entryPath, entryStyle, trailingNewline, write, writeNote, envRef, homeEnv, xdgConfig. tk writes only `configFiles.user`; `project` and `managedFiles` are listed so tk can refuse them.

harnesses.name: Claude Code
harnesses.listChanged: interactive sessions refetch; -p and SDK refresh the list only
harnesses.allowlist: managed settings: allowedMcpServers entries {serverUrl} (exact or * wildcards) or {serverCommand} (the exact argv, env not compared); a serverName entry is not a security control; allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true makes the managed list the only one (V, managed-mcp docs)
harnesses.notes: ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expand in command, args, env, url and headers, user scope included; an unset variable stays literal with a warning in claude mcp list; some credential variable names read as empty in a remote server's url and headers (V, code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, read 27 Oct). Reserved server names are skipped at load (V, same page). Probe run 27 Oct (2.1.311, `claude mcp get` starting a stdio server with TOKEN set): ${TOKEN} expanded in env and in args (V). add-json writes the object as given, appends the key at the end of mcpServers, rewrites the whole file with JSON.stringify(_, null, 2) and no final newline, and refuses an existing name with exit 1 (V, recorded with 2.1.311). tk keeps the rest of the file byte for byte; Claude Code would re-indent a file not in its own format.

harnesses.name: Codex CLI
harnesses.toolNameForm: each server is one Responses API namespace `mcp__<server>` holding function tools named by the tool; hooks still see the flat `mcp__<server>__<tool>` (V, rust-v0.164.0 core/src/tools/handlers/mcp.rs#L145, #L565; PR #17404, commit 0df7e9a8, 15 Apr 2026). Rules case 21
harnesses.nameMangling: server and tool names: every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_] becomes _; collisions get _ plus 12 hex of SHA-1; namespace + name capped at 128 bytes (V, codex-mcp/src/tools.rs#L113-L237). Server names in config allow [A-Za-z0-9-_:@/.] (V, cli/src/mcp_cmd.rs#L1144)
harnesses.listChanged: behind feature mcp_tool_list_changed, under development and off by default: tools do not refresh (V, features/src/lib.rs#L1598 at rust-v0.164.0)
harnesses.notes: codex mcp add (0.163.0) appends `[mcp_servers.<name>]` with a blank line before it, keeps comments and other keys, and silently replaces an existing name (V, recorded). `--env K=V` writes the value literally into `[mcp_servers.<name>.env]`, so tk passes variables by name instead: `env_vars = ["NAME"]`, and `env_http_headers` / `http_headers` tables for headers; `codex mcp get` (0.163.0) reads all three back (V, run 27 Oct). Codex ignores unknown keys in an entry silently (V, run), so a misspelt key fails open; tk writes only these keys. An entry can also carry `http_headers_helper`, a program Codex runs; tk never writes it. At rust-v0.164.0 the source has deny_unknown_fields on RawMcpServerConfig (config/src/mcp_types.rs#L373), which disagrees with the 0.163.0 run that accepted an unknown key; tk writes only known keys either way. CODEX_HOME must name an existing folder (utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs#L5-L17). No ${VAR} interpolation exists in Codex config (NF); variables are named through env_vars, bearer_token_env_var and env_http_headers (V). When Codex rewrites the file it sorts env and header tables by key and replaces a non-inline server table whole (V, core/src/config/edit/document_helpers.rs).

harnesses.nameMangling: mcp_ is prepended, [^a-zA-Z0-9_\-.:] becomes _, a leading non-letter gets _; over 63 characters the name becomes the first 30 + ... + the last 30 (V, core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts#L722-L750 at v0.65.0). The policy parser splits at the first _ after mcp_, so no _ in server names (V, docs/tools/mcp-server.md#L692)

harnesses.notes: gemini mcp add (0.65.0) writes command, args (always, [] when none), env and url, type, headers; it keeps comments and ends the file with no newline (V, recorded). Probe run 27 Oct (`gemini mcp list` with folder trust off, starting a stdio server): both $TOKEN and ${TOKEN} expand in env and args (V). User-level servers are suppressed in an untrusted folder (V, `gemini mcp list` warning). Source (v0.65.0): $VAR, ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expand across the whole settings object (V, cli/src/utils/envVarResolver.ts); a url with no type means streamable HTTP with an SSE fallback, which disagrees with the docs' "bare url means SSE" (V both; tk always writes type); per-server enablement lives in ~/.gemini/mcp-server-enablement.json; `gemini mcp add` defaults to project scope (-s user needed). GEMINI_CLI_HOME replaces the home folder, not ~/.gemini (V, core/src/utils/paths.ts#L13-L28); tk does not follow it. System files move with GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH.

harnesses.notes: copilot mcp add (1.0.104) writes tools ["*"], type local, command, args, env or tools, type http, url, headers, with a final newline (V, recorded). Schema (bundled api.schema.json): stdio {command, args, cwd, env, type stdio|local}, remote {url, type http|sse, headers, oauth*}, plus tools, excludeTools, timeout ms, deferTools, displayName (V). A value that starts with $ is read as a reference to an environment variable (V for the changelog entry, github.com/github/copilot-cli changelog.md#L3447; I that it holds at 1.0.104; not probed, since `copilot mcp list` starts no server). So tk writes $VAR as a whole value only and refuses a header such as Bearer ${VAR} for Copilot. COPILOT_HOME or --config-dir replaces ~/.copilot (V, cli-main.js). Enable/disable is a persisted list, not a key. It also reads .mcp.json and .github/mcp.json in a workspace.
